LESSON: MICROORGANISMS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Life Science
Topic 1.7: Microorganisms
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 13

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Microorganisms, part of Life Science in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How are microorganisms important in day to day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify microorganisms that affect human beings,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Microorganisms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain modes of transmission of microorganisms in human beings,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Microorganisms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. identify types of infections caused by microorganisms in human beings,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Microorganisms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. describe methods of control and prevention of infections caused by microorganisms,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Microorganisms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. explain the economic importance of microorganisms,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Microorganisms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. appreciate the effect of microorganisms in day to day life.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Microorganisms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify microorganisms that affect human beings,

   Microorganisms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. explain modes of transmission of microorganisms in human beings,

   Microorganisms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. identify types of infections caused by microorganisms in human beings,

   Microorganisms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. describe methods of control and prevention of infections caused by microorganisms,

   Microorganisms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. explain the economic importance of microorganisms,

   Microorganisms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. appreciate the effect of microorganisms in day to day life.

   Microorganisms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

G. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss types of microorganisms that affect human beings (fungi, bacteria and viruses) and share with peers. Learners with speech difficulties could use Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) to identify the types of organisms that affect human beings,

2. use digital or print media to search for information on the modes of transmission of microorganisms in human beings and present in the plenary. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or adapted digital devices to conduct research. Regulate screen resolution appropriately for learners who are sensitive to light,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss types of microorganisms that affect human beings (fungi, bacteria and viruses) and share with peers. Learners with speech difficulties could use Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) to identify the types of organisms that affect human beings,
2. use digital or print media to search for information on the modes of transmission of microorganisms in human beings and present in the plenary. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or adapted digital devices to conduct research. Regulate screen resolution appropriately for learners who are sensitive to light,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Microorganisms together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: as the learner uses digital devices to research on infections caused by microorganisms as well as their

control and prevention mechanisms.

● Communication and collaboration: as the learner shares information gathered on types of microorganism infections, control

and prevention.

Values:
Respect: as the learner becomes considerate of others’ opinion while discussing methods of controlling and preventing

microorganism infections.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Socio-economic issues- Poverty eradication: as the learner sensitises the community on the significance of food preservation

and the economic importance of microorganisms.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Text book, Food substrates (such as bread, fruits, vegetables), Local environment, Plastic bags, Lab apparatus such as Petri dish,

Online resources, educational videos, interactive simulations, adapted digital devices, Adapted writing resources,

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify microorganisms that affect human beings,
2. explain modes of transmission of microorganisms in human beings,
3. identify types of infections caused by microorganisms in human beings,
4. describe methods of control and prevention of infections caused by microorganisms,
5. explain the economic importance of microorganisms,
6. appreciate the effect of microorganisms in day to day life.

Remember the key question: How are microorganisms important in day to day life?
